title: Pancreatic safety of incretin-based drugs: FDA and EMA assessment
authors: Egan AG, Blind E, Dunder K, de Graeff PA, Hummer BT, Bourcier T, et al.
funder: not stated; the article reports the assessments of the US Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency
result: FDA re-evaluated more than 250 toxicology studies in nearly 18,000 healthy animals and found no overt pancreatic toxic effects or pancreatitis and no drug-induced pancreatic tumours over 2 years; in a high-fat-diet mouse model exenatide for 12 weeks produced minimal-to-moderate exacerbation of acinar-cell hyperplasia, atrophy and periductal inflammation or fibrosis, a model the agencies called not definitively qualified but meriting investigation. The clinical review covered more than 200 trials with about 41,000 participants. Both agencies stated that assertions of a causal association with pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer were inconsistent with the current data, that they had not reached a final conclusion, and that pancreatitis would continue to be considered a risk of these drugs. Observational studies had yielded inconsistent results with limited power, inadequate outcome validation and inadequate confounding control.
